independent_findings.reason: This is an explicitly authored Canonical Library Node B. The arbitrary measurable carrier and base measure are a library generalization, not a claim that the Gaussian paper states such a theorem. A new source-Anchor graph is not needed for this bounded scope review.

The common base measure need not be finite, a probability measure or sigma-finite. The functions themselves are nonnegative, measurable, genuinely integrable and normalized to mass one. All stated event integrals and comparisons are mathematically meaningful under those conditions; no product/Fubini requirement is introduced.

Carrier, measurable structure, measure and functions fix the objects. Nonnegativity, measurability, L1 and unit integrals are the intrinsic density contract of this generic theorem. None assumes affinity L1/range, event-TV equality or either desired comparison. The seal's SOURCE label is understood only as an intrinsic premise of this authored generic statement, not a paper-derived hypothesis or added Gaussian premise.
independent_findings.qualification: Pointwise nonnegativity and Measurable are stronger presentation choices than their a.e./a.e.-measurable variants. They are explicit and suitable for the chosen actual Gaussian representatives; this is not a claim of the weakest possible interface.

independent_findings.reason: a is exactly the real sqrt-product integral; genuine Integrable is an output. delta is the supremum of absolute differences of actual measurable-event set integrals. It carries normalized TV semantics only after the theorem proves half-L1 and the actual-law consumer proves its event-mass identification. No RN derivative choice, default probability law or unrelated TV surrogate is hidden in the signature.

The half-L1 factor 1/2, lower bound 1-a and upper bound sqrt(1-a^2) use the same affinity normalization a=integral sqrt(f*g). Both inequalities are compatible with 0<=a<=1. There is no extra factor 2 or change to the Gaussian Eq25 constants.

The conclusions form one coherent normalized-density bridge: genuine affinity L1/range, event-sup/half-L1 correspondence and two-sided TV-affinity comparison. They require real analysis and measurable-event reasoning and are not repackaged public premises. Including both sides is justified by the two bounded source-consumer roles; no product law, Gaussian spectral result, query model or main lower bound is absorbed.

TechnicalLemmas/InformationTheory is the appropriate shared home for this carrier-generic theorem rather than a paper-private copy. The seal/frontier record a prior Samplinglib/Mathlib reuse search and proposed primitive reuse. This reviewer did not inspect API or implementation bodies and therefore does not independently certify exhaustive absence of an existing equivalent theorem or correctness of the named API contracts. The mathematical shape is substantive rather than a wrapper; final implementation canonicality still depends on actual primitive reuse and no duplicate exported copies.

The Gaussian seal hash is unchanged and its source-facing signature retains only n>=3 and kappa>=4. Generic density hypotheses belong to the shared theorem; the actual Gaussian proof must obtain them internally from actual_mixture_densities and identify each event set integral with the same actual Ppos/Pneg event mass before using the upper comparison and B.7.

Applying the generic result to actual full product densities is a valid intended use only after separate actual-product density and normalization proofs. Neither the generic theorem nor this review proves product-affinity=a^k, residual Gaussian coordinates, tensorization or amplified TV. Prove genuine affinity integrability and range from the density contract; establish all square-root algebra, L2/cross-product integrability and radicand signs before integral and scalar manipulations.

Prove the lower and upper comparisons with the sealed normalization and every needed integrability/positivity condition; do not assume either comparison in a helper exported as a theorem premise.

Check actual named primitive/API contracts, reuse them where compatible, keep internal providers minimal and avoid duplicate generic paper-route declarations. This review is not an API-body or exhaustive reuse audit.
